extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent applicants / patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examining and assessing means- (or step-) plus-function claim limitations under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) (pre‑AIA 112 sixth paragraph), and for determining whether the specification discloses corresponding structure, material, acts, or algorithms sufficient to avoid indefiniteness, lack of written description, or lack of enablement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to disclose corresponding structure for means-plus-function under 35 U.S.C. 112(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: The recited “means” for performing the specified function shall be construed to cover the corresponding “structure or material” described in the specification and equivalents thereof; examiners must determine whether the written description discloses the corresponding structure, material, or acts that perform the claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no corresponding structure is disclosed (e.g., the limitation is only supported by software without an algorithm and the computer/microprocessor programmed with the algorithm), the limitation should be deemed indefinite and rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (or pre‑AIA 112, second paragraph). See MPEP § 2163.03; determine claimed function then review the written description/drawings/figures/sequence listing for corresponding structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithm disclosure requirement for computer-implemented means-plus-function claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For computer-implemented means-plus-function limitations, the specification must explicitly disclose an algorithm (a sequence of steps) corresponding to the claimed function; merely reciting the function or outcome is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An algorithm must be a sequence of steps; implicit or inherent disclosure of a class of algorithms is not sufficient and a ‘one-step’ pseudo‑algorithm is insufficient. Case law: Blackboard; Noah; Encyc. Brittanica v. Alpine; Biomedino; Atmel. Code fragments that only return error messages or do not explain how to perform an essential action are inadequate (Media Rights example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple claimed functions require disclosure of corresponding structure for each function
rubrics_metrics.description: When a means-plus-function limitation performs multiple identifiable functions, the specification must disclose adequate corresponding structure/algorithm to perform all of the claimed functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the specification discloses an algorithm that accomplishes only one of multiple functions, the disclosure is treated as if it disclosed no algorithm and the limitation is indefinite (see Noah, Williamson, Media Rights). Examiners should verify that structure/algorithms for each recited function are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode of implementation limits claim scope (hardware vs. software)
rubrics_metrics.description: By choosing a means-plus-function limitation and invoking 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the applicant limits that claim element to the disclosed structure (e.g., hardware or combination of hardware and software) and equivalents; examiners should not construe the limitation as covering pure software implementation unless the specification discloses corresponding structure for software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the limitation is only supported by software and there is no corresponding algorithm/structure disclosed, treat as indefinite under 112(b). Claims should be read as a whole to determine whether the claim as a whole is directed to software per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear linkage / association requirement between disclosed structure and claimed function
rubrics_metrics.description: The structure disclosed in the written description is the corresponding structure only if the written description or the prosecution history clearly links or associates that structure to the function recited in the means/step-plus-function limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This linkage is the quid pro quo for employing 112(f). If one of ordinary skill in the art cannot identify what structure, material, or acts disclosed performs the claimed function, a rejection under 112(b) is appropriate. See B. Braun; Medical Instrumentation & Diagnostics; Telcordia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and figures as written description (but not incorporated-by-reference material)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings, figures, tables, or sequence listings may provide the written description of corresponding structure, material, or acts, but structure disclosed only in material incorporated by reference or in prior art references cannot be relied upon as the specification disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office personnel must review only the specification itself (and not rely on incorporated documents) to determine whether one skilled in the art would identify corresponding structure. See Vas-Cath; Pressure Prods.; Atmel guidance on incorporated material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three common situations warranting a 112(b) rejection for means-plus-function limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (or pre‑AIA 112 second paragraph) may be appropriate when: (1) it is unclear whether a claim limitation invokes 112(f); (2) 112(f) is invoked and there is no or insufficient disclosure of structure/material/acts for the claimed function; and/or (3) 112(f) is invoked and the supporting disclosure fails to clearly link or associate the disclosed structure/material/acts to the claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should apply the 3‑prong analysis and determine whether 112(f) applies, then whether disclosure and linkage are present. Ambiguous claim language may render the 3‑prong analysis inconclusive, warranting rejection. Applicant can rebut or amend during prosecution to clarify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure for evaluating whether 112(f) applies and for identifying corresponding structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a limitation is determined to invoke 112(f), the examiner should identify the claimed function and then review the written description (including drawings, figures, tables, sequence listings) to determine whether the corresponding structure/material/acts that perform the function are disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the claims, specification, and how a person of ordinary skill would understand the claims in view of the disclosure. If examiner cannot identify corresponding structure, make a rejection under 112(b) or require information under 37 CFR 1.105 to compel identification. See MPEP § 704.11(a) Example R and § 704.12 for replies to requirements for information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of incorporated-by-reference material and applicant amendment options
rubrics_metrics.description: If corresponding structure is described only in broad generic terms with specifics incorporated by reference, the examiner must evaluate the specification itself (without relying on the incorporated document) to see if one skilled in the art could identify corresponding structure; if not, applicant must amend the specification to include relevant portions of the referenced document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is not required to insert entire referenced documents—only the relevant portions corresponding to the means/step-plus-function limitation. See 37 CFR 1.57(d)(3) and Default Proof Credit Card System guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit disclosure: examiner may require explicit clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the written description only implicitly or inherently sets forth the structure/materials/acts corresponding to a means-plus-function element and the examiner concludes one skilled in the art would recognize what performs the function, the examiner should have the applicant clarify the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should either amend the written description to expressly recite what structure/materials/acts perform the function, or the examiner should state on the record what those structures/materials/acts are. This should be done in a manner that does not add new matter. See 37 CFR 1.75(d) and MPEP § 608.01(o).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere recitation of function insufficient for written description and enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: Merely restating the function associated with a means-plus-function limitation in the specification, without more description of the means to accomplish it, is insufficient to provide corresponding structure for definiteness and will likely fail to satisfy written description and enablement under 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases: Noah; Blackboard; Aristocrat. 37 CFR 1.75(d)(1) requires terms in claims to find clear support or antecedent basis in the description. Distinguish between describing the outcome (insufficient) and describing the means/structure to achieve it (required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interplay: indefiniteness often signals lack of written description/enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: A means-plus-function limitation found indefinite under 112(b) for failure to disclose sufficient corresponding structure (e.g., computer plus algorithm) will also likely lack adequate written description under 112(a) and may not be enabled for the full scope of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should consider both written description and enablement requirements when assessing means-plus-function limitations. See MPEP §§ 2163.03, 2161.01, and 2164.08. The enablement inquiry is separate from written description and examines whether one skilled in the art could make and use the full scope of the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional/structural material not recited in claim should not be imported unless necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional limitations not expressly recited in the claim, or structural limitations in the specification that are unnecessary to perform the claimed function, cannot be imported into the claim during claim construction under 112(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not read extraneous structural or functional limitations from the specification into the claim unless they are the corresponding structure necessary to perform the recited function. See Welker Bearing; Wenger Mfg.

rubrics_metrics.name: One skilled artisan's ability to implement does not substitute for corresponding-structure disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that a person of ordinary skill in the art might be able to design a program or means to carry out the recited function (enablement issue) does not relieve the patentee of the duty to disclose sufficient corresponding structure in the specification for a means-plus-function limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inquiry under 112(f) is whether the specification contains a sufficiently precise description of the corresponding structure—not whether a skilled artisan could devise some means. See Blackboard; Atmel; EON Corp.; Biomedino distinctions between enablement and corresponding-structure analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and examiner actions when applicant does not identify corresponding structure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner cannot identify corresponding structure/material/acts, the examiner should reject the claim under 112(b); the examiner may also issue a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 to require identification of the corresponding structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a 1.105 requirement is made and applicant states they lack the information or fails to identify the corresponding structure, a 112(b) rejection should be made. Failure to reply to such requirements can result in abandonment. See MPEP § 704.11(a) Example R and § 704.12 on replies to requirements for information.
